body:
`NDFrame._clip_with_one_bound` converts a non-`Series` list-like bound via `_align_for_op(threshold, axis, flex=None)` and passes the result to `where`. Since GH-61828 that routes an extension-dtype operand through `_maybe_align_series_as_frame`, which now returns an EA-columned `DataFrame` instead of the `Series` it used to return. `DataFrame.where` has an EA-aware column-wise path for a 1-D `other` but none for a 2-D one, so the bound interleaves to an object ndarray.

```python
df = pd.DataFrame([[10, 20], [30, 40]])

df.clip(lower=pd.array([15, 25], dtype="Int64"), axis=1).dtypes
# object, object   (int64, int64 before GH-61828)

df.clip(lower=pd.array([15, 25], dtype="Int64"), axis=1, inplace=True)
# TypeError: Invalid value '[[15]]' for dtype 'int64'
```

`_align_for_op` now skips that broadcast when `flex is None` — clip is that flag's only caller — so the bound stays a `Series` and takes the working 1-D path. `_clip_with_one_bound` then pins `axis=1` when it gets a `Series` back with `axis=None`, since `_align_for_op` had already aligned the bound against `self.columns` and `DataFrame.align(Series, axis=None)` raises.

The object degradation never shipped. Against released 3.0, the `clip` changes are that `inplace=True` with an extension-dtype array/`Index` bound no longer writes wrong values (3.0 applied the bound along the wrong axis), and omitting `axis` no longer raises `ValueError: Must specify axis=0 or 1`.

A `SparseArray` bound on an integer-dtype frame still raises `AttributeError` in `np_can_hold_element`; that is fixed separately in GH-68457.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5 (high)`), which diagnosed the regression, wrote the fix and tests, and ran a differential sweep against released 3.0.
title: BUG: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array/Index bound degrades to object
